observations: In this session I opened assets/panels/03-1.png twice with Read (in the first pass and again now), along with checkin-patients.png, main-cast.png, vision-cast.png and the re-rendered workflow/review/page-03.png. The panel hash in this request (6dab121e...) matches the previous request. That fits the art being unchanged, but my judgement comes from viewing the image, not from the hash.

Mr. Raman matches his sheet: white hair, bushy white brows, round glasses, prominent ears, smile lines, a cream half-sleeve shirt and grey trousers. His near (right) hand grips the wooden walking stick and his far (left) hand rests on the counter, as production specifies.
Meera types with both hands on the keyboard. The monitor is angled toward her, so only its back shows. Her braid, bangle and blue kurta match her sheet, and she greets him warmly.

The background has a QR stand with an abstract block pattern, a wall TV with a teal screen and an empty white strip, a vitals table with a small monitor showing abstract blocks, and two waiting patients seen from behind in grey and dark brown. None of it shows readable text or numbers.

Cheek dot: a small dark dot is visible just below the outer corner of Meera's right eye (screen-left), on her upper cheek. I could only view the image at the size Read displays it; I could not view it at 200% myself.

Her sheet has no mole. Her design traits are round eyes with a visible lower lash line, thin high brows, and a round face with a left-cheek dimple when smiling. The dot is therefore off-model. It also falls where the vision-scene partner's design has a small mole under the right eye. Priya's beauty spot is above the lip, a different place.

My judgement on the dot: it does not matter for identity in this panel. All three of Meera's traits are clearly present, along with her side braid, blue kurta, bangle and reception desk. The partner appears only in the pale-blue vision vignette, with wavy shoulder-length hair and a mustard kurta, so nobody would confuse the two. At page scale the dot is about one or two pixels and barely noticeable. I did not see the dot on Meera in 01-2, 01-3, 02-3, 02-4 or 03-3, so it is a one-off stray mark, not a new trait. It can optionally be removed with a local edit later, but it does not block this pass.

Page-03.png: the refitted caption now ends above Mr. Raman's head, with a visible gap of wall between the box and his hair. It covers only the empty upper wall and the left part of the background TV. Both faces, the stick hand, the counter hand, Meera's typing hands and the monitor are uncovered.
